title: Affine base change gives a morphism of affine etale sites
statement: Let $h:T'\to T$ be an affine morphism of schemes [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. For the affine etale sites of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-site-topos], the functor $u:T_{affine,\Et}\to T'_{affine,\Et}$ sending $V\to T$ to $V\times_TT'\to T'$ is well defined: the fibre product is affine and etale over $T'$. It is continuous, and its induced inverse-image/direct-image adjunction on sheaves of sets is a morphism of sites $g:T'_{affine,\Et}\to T_{affine,\Et}$.

proof.text: Let $V\to T$ be an object of $T_{affine,\Et}$. The base change $V\times_TT'\to T'$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits](1). It is affine as a scheme: the projection $V\times_TT'\to V$ is the base change of the affine map $h$ and is therefore affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1); its target $V$ is affine, so its source is affine by (2) of that node. On arrows use the ordinary base-change functor of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits](1). Thus it restricts to the claimed functor $u$ on the full subcategories of affine objects. Lean realization: Scheme.affineEtaleBaseChange_isAffine is proved directly by Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.instIsAffinePullbackSchemeOfIsAffineHom_1, using the affine-object property of V and IsAffineHom h. The definition restricts ordinary base change with ObjectProperty.lift. Steps 2–4 are realized by the proved private helper AlgebraicGeometry.affineEtaleBaseChange_cover_pullback_continuous and the theorem AlgebraicGeometry.affineEtaleSiteBaseChange.

proof.text: Base change a finite family of affine etale objects using Scheme.affineEtaleBaseChange. Presieve.map_ofArrows identifies its image family. For each arrow, MorphismProperty.Over.isPullback_map_left and MorphismProperty.of_isPullback give etaleness. Given a point x of the target pullback, joint surjectivity of the original family gives a point y above pullback.fst(x). Scheme.exists_preimage_of_isPullback lifts the pair (y,x) to a point of the corresponding source pullback. Thus the same finite index set gives a covering after base change (the pointwise realization of lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change). For pullbacks, show that affineness of etale objects is closed under WalkingCospan limits, using Scheme.isAffine_of_isLimit and the forgetful functor to schemes. Hence the affine inclusion preserves pullbacks and the fully faithful target inclusion reflects them. Full etale base change preserves finite limits by lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits. Its restriction therefore preserves pullbacks by preservesLimitsOfShape_of_reflects_of_preserves.

proof.text: Use fullAffineEtalePrecoverage_isPretopology of def-weil-pbc-full-affine-etale-site. The topology generated by its underlying precoverage equals the pretopology topology: one inclusion follows from toGrothendieck_le_iff_le_toPrecoverage, the other from upward closure of covering sieves. Test the sheaf condition on the pretopology coverings with Presieve.isSheaf_pretopology. Pullback preservation identifies the matching-family condition with that of the image covering via Presieve.IsSheafFor.comp_iff_of_preservesPairwisePullbacks; Step 2 and the sheaf condition on the target give continuity. The sheafified Kan-extension adjunction is then Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafAdjunctionContinuous, realizing lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction.

Instantiate lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-restriction-unit with U=Scheme.affineEtaleBaseChange, the definitional identity U(h) followed by affine inclusion = affine inclusion followed by full etale base change, the continuity of Step 3 for every affine h, and the constructed sheaf adjunction. Its comparison e identifies full inverse image followed by restriction rho_Tprime with rho_T followed by affine inverse image L. Restriction rho is an equivalence in Type (u+1) by lem-stage3-affine-etale-restriction-large-sets (the required universe of the affine-topos comparison). Full inverse image preserves finite limits by lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-exact. Thus rho_T composed with L preserves finite limits, by preservesFiniteLimits_of_natIso applied to e. Precompose with the inverse equivalence of rho_T, which preserves finite limits, and use the counit isomorphism to identify the composite with L. Finally the constructed adjunction makes L a left adjoint, so it preserves finite colimits. Combine this with Steps 2 and 3 to obtain exactly the stated conjunction.
